sentences.text: This miscellaneous appeal has been filed by the appellant under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, being aggrieved by award dated 27.01.2023 passed by 26th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jabalpur in MACC No.4722/2019 for enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: 26th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that Tribunal has wrongly determined permanent disability as 20%, whereas, it should have been at least 40%.
The appellant was working as labour and permanent disability suffered by the appellant is in relation to right leg.

Accordingly,
appropriate amount be enhanced with respect to permanent disability.
3. Learned counsel for the respondent/Insurance Company submits that Tribunal has rightly determined appellant's permanent disability and it can be enhanced maximum to 25% and not more than that.

Further, relying on Oriental Insurance Company Limited Vs. Smt. Champavati Ray,
Guhati High Court, it is urged that no interest should be awarded on amount granted under future prospect.

entities.text:
Oriental Insurance Company Limited Vs. Smt. Champavati Ray,
Guhati High Court
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

5. So far as percentage of permanent disability is concerned, as per para 32 of impugned award,
appellant was working as labourer and thereby, earning his livelihood.
As per para 22-26 of impugned award, appellant has suffered injuries/fracture/ permanent disability in right leg.

Hence,
in view of nature of injuries/part of body, nature of disability and nature of profession/job of appellant, in this Court's considered opinion, functional disability is assessed as 50% and not 20%.

There is no dispute with respect to income, future prospects and multiplier etc.
6.

If loss of earning capacity is calculated by taking appellant's monthly income as Rs.7,700/- per month, then, annual income comes to Rs.92,400/- (Rs.7,700/- x 12) and if 40% future prospects is added, then, amount comes to Rs.1,29,340/-.
There is 50% permanent disability.
Hence, annual loss of future earnings would be Rs.64,820/-.
After applying multiplier of 18, total loss of future earning capacity comes to Rs.11,66,760/-.
7. Therefore, appellant is entitled to receive Rs.11,66,760/- as loss of future earning capacity whereas Tribunal has awarded Rs.4,65,696/- for loss of earning capacity.
8. Learned counsel for the respondent/Insurance Company after relying on Oriental Insurance Company Ltd.(supra) submits that no interest can be awarded for future prospect.
In this Court's considered opinion, there is no cross objection/appeal on behalf of Insurance Company.

Therefore,
above issue cannot be gone into in the instant appeal and above submissions of learned counsel for the respondent are negated.
9. In view of above, appellant is entitled to receive enhanced amount of Rs.7,01,064/- for loss of earning capacity over and above awarded by the Tribunal.
Amount awarded by the Tribunal under other heads shall remain same.

sentences.text: Enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate awarded by Tribunal.
Other findings of the tribunal shall remain intact.
11. Appellant has valued present appeal Rs.3,00,000/-, therefore, appellants shall pay deficit Court fees on remaining amount within three months.
The appellant shall be entitled to receive enhance amount, only after payment of deficit Court fees.
12. Accordingly, appeal filed by the appellant is partly allowed to the extent indicated herein above.
